questions.q: What does `--resource-group data-platform-dev` control in an `az deployment group create` command?
options: The scope — this deployment can only create, update, or delete resources inside that resource group, never outside it
Which Azure region the CLI itself runs in
The name of the Bicep file being deployed
The subscription's billing tier
questions.explain: Every deployment targets a scope, and a resource-group deployment is bounded to that one resource group.

options: Reports exactly what would be created, modified, or left unchanged, without actually touching anything
Immediately applies the deployment and then asks for confirmation afterward
Deletes all resources in the target resource group
Has no effect — it's ignored by the Azure CLI
questions.explain: This is Bicep's version of the review-before-you-commit idea that Terraform's plan step gives, one flag earlier in the deployment process.

questions.q: What does VS Code's deployment pane actually show, and is it a different deployment mechanism from the CLI?
options: Live progress per resource — it's a convenience over the CLI, running the exact same az deployment group create call underneath
It shows only a final success/failure message with no progress detail
It's a completely separate deployment engine unrelated to the Azure CLI
It only works for Terraform deployments, not Bicep
questions.explain: Under the hood, VS Code's Deploy Bicep File command runs the same az deployment group create call as the CLI.

questions.q: When would you use `az deployment sub create` instead of `az deployment group create`?
options: For something that lives above any single resource group, like the resource group itself
Every single deployment in this course should use sub create instead
Only when deploying an Azure SQL database specifically
There is no real difference between the two commands
questions.explain: A resource-group deployment is the right scope for almost everything in this course, since a storage account, Event Hub, or Azure SQL server all live inside one.

questions.q: What do the parameters supplied via `--parameters` in the deploy command correspond to?
options: The `param` declarations inside the Bicep file, from Lesson 13
Environment variables set on the local machine only
Values hardcoded permanently inside the .bicep file
Nothing in the Bicep file — they're only used by the CLI itself
questions.explain: `--parameters` supplies exactly the values a file's `param` declarations expect, either inline or from a .bicepparam file.
